title: Mercury: The Scorched Survivor
objective: After this level you can describe Mercury’s extreme temperatures and its lack of atmosphere.
summary: The smallest, innermost planet has almost no air, so it bakes by day and freezes by night, yet keeps ice at its poles.

cards.headline: The planet closest to the Sun has ice on it.
Small, fast and close
cards.body: Mercury is the smallest planet and the closest to the Sun. It races around its orbit in just 88 Earth days, the shortest year in the solar system.

cards.headline: No blanket
cards.body: Mercury has almost no atmosphere to hold heat. Its surface reaches about 430 °C in the day, then plunges to about −180 °C at night, one of the biggest temperature swings of any planet.

cards.fact: Mercury has ice in craters near its poles.
cards.context: The floors of some polar craters are always in shadow. Sunlight never reaches them, so water ice survives on the planet closest to the Sun.

cards.headline: Mercury: surveyed
learned: Mercury is the smallest planet and closest to the Sun
Its year is only 88 Earth days

questions.prompt: Which is the smallest planet in the solar system?

options.label: Pluto, beyond Neptune
options.rationale: Pluto is classified as a dwarf planet.

questions.explanation: Mercury is the smallest planet, and the closest to the Sun.

questions.prompt: Why does Mercury get so cold at night despite being so close to the Sun?

options.label: It has almost no atmosphere to hold in heat
It moves away from the Sun every night
options.rationale: Night is about which side faces the Sun.

options.label: Its surface is covered in reflective ice
options.rationale: Ice exists only in shadowed polar craters.

options.label: The Sun switches off on its far side

questions.explanation: Without an atmosphere to trap heat, Mercury’s surface loses its warmth quickly once the Sun sets.

questions.prompt: From Level 3: Venus stays scorching all night, but Mercury freezes. What makes the difference?

options.label: Venus spins much faster than Mercury
Venus is closer to the Sun than Mercury
Mercury’s ice cools the whole planet
options.rationale: The ice is only in shadowed craters.

options.label: Venus has a thick heat-trapping atmosphere; Mercury has almost none

questions.explanation: Venus’s thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat day and night. Mercury has almost no atmosphere, so its heat escapes.
